idiom_name: Handlebars registered helpers / Express app.locals function locals
implementation_notes: Helpers are functions plugged into the engine: Handlebars.registerHelper(name, fn) registers value helpers and block helpers (options.fn / options.inverse for the wrapped block, Handlebars.SafeString for markup), while Express exposes helper functions to every template through app.locals and per-request values through res.locals - the Express documentation names providing helper functions to templates as the purpose. The J2EE helper class has no reason to exist here: a function plus a registry entry is the whole structure, and retrieval stays in the route handler or middleware that fills the locals. A module or class is justified only when the helper needs configuration shared across views (a pre-configured locale formatter).
pitfalls: Helpers registered on the default Handlebars instance are global to the process, so two apps or two tests share them; create a scoped environment (Handlebars.create()) when that matters.
A helper returning a Promise renders as [object Promise]; helpers are synchronous unless the engine has an async mode.
Handlebars.SafeString and the triple-stache {{{ }}} both disable escaping - use them only for markup you constructed, never for user data.
A registered helper shadows a context field of the same name, so {{money}} stops meaning the data property once the helper exists.
